answer.rationale: Competitive price cut and doubled churn conversations in SMB segment create immediate retention risk. memory_73 demonstrates targeted promotional pricing generates strong acquisition and revenue lift in price-sensitive SMB cohort without documented harm to LTV. memory_31 confirms SMB respond to targeted interventions. However, promotional pricing carries downstream risk: it may train price-sensitive customers toward expectation of discounts, risking margin compression and future churn when promotions end. This risk is material but is outweighed by acute competitive threat to existing revenue base today. A standard_experiment scope (time-limited, cohort-specific pricing for churn-at-risk SMB accounts) allows validation of revenue stabilization while preserving ability to shift strategy if margin impact becomes unacceptable. memory_44 and memory_57 suggest enterprise and referral levers exist but are slower-acting and insufficient as sole response to acute SMB retention crisis. Preserving uncertainty: we acknowledge promotional pricing may not replicate exp_73 results in this specific competitive context, and margin/churn rebound effects are not fully quantified in prior work.
